data_quality_notes:
WHAT THIS REPORT IS: a Saturday run, so it is almost entirely position management and week-ahead preparation. 20 of the 21 recommendations are decisions on the existing 20-position book — 5 closes (TLT, CEG, FCX, ITA, ITB), 2 trims (XLE, KHC) and 13 holds — and SLB is the only new entry. Every equity price is the Friday 2026-10-23 close, re-fetched this morning and confirmed unchanged; that is a closed market, not stale data, and no live equity print exists until Monday 09:30 ET. Entries are for the 2026-10-26 open. Research ran 06:01-06:37 ET inside the pre-open window and was NOT truncated.

READ THE FIVE CLOSES FIRST, AND EXPECT VALIDATION TO FAIL THEM. TLT, CEG, FCX, ITA and ITB all carry negative expectancy (-1.4pp to -6.4pp against their own break-even), and CEG (1.39 ATR), ITB (1.56) and ITA (1.69) also fail the stop-distance floor measured from entry. Those failures ARE the recommendation: a negative expectancy and a sub-floor stop are what 'this position is no longer worth holding' looks like in numbers. The schema has no way to say 'close this', so the instruction lives in catalyst.action and exit.scale_plan on rows that still carry their original levels. Because --enforce will demote them to the watchlist, each close instruction has been pre-written into the watchlist as well so it survives the demotion. No win probability was raised to make any row pass, and none should be.

THREE HOLDS ARE ALSO EXPECTED TO FAIL, and their instructions are likewise pre-seeded on the watchlist. IYR's stop is 1.75 ATR from entry against the 1.8 ETF floor and DG's is 1.99 against a 2.0 stock floor — both were published below floor on earlier runs, both are real defects, and both are stated rather than fixed, since widening a live position's stop is an amendment this run has no new information to justify. HII fails the 2.5 long-term reward-to-risk floor at 2.15. It is published failed rather than tuned, and it is published rather than dropped for one reason: it is an open position whose anchors changed today, and dropping the row would leave the position graded against the superseded 430.00 target. It holds existing exposure only and does not clear the bar for new capital.

LONG-TERM ANCHORS WERE RE-DERIVED TODAY FROM FETCHED FUNDAMENTALS, which changed three ratios. BCC: target 110.00 to 124.50 (revenue/share 183.32 x the 6.79% five-year net margin = 12.45 normalized EPS at a mid-cycle 10x) and bear case 63.00 to 58.00 (book value/share 57.99), giving 2.59 against the 2.5 floor. The target moved UP, which is exactly the inflation this repo polices; the defence is that the bear case moved DOWN in the same pass, against the idea's own interest, and that BCC's qualification is knife-edge on the multiple — 10x passes at 2.59, 9x fails at 1.92, and it needs roughly 9.8x. Treat the multiple as the live question. PFE: bear case 24.50 to 23.26 (12x the 1.94 normalized EPS), worsening the ratio from 4.65 to 3.32, which still passes — the point of doing it. HII: as above, and the honest finding there is that the ratio spans 1.8 to 5.3 across defensible assumptions, so the apparent precision of a '430 target' was false.

RATIOS CLUSTERED NEAR THE FLOOR: 8 of the 18 swing ideas recompute between 2.00 and 2.20, with TLT at exactly 2.00. That is the signature of targets fitted to clear the bar, and it is flagged rather than explained away. The mitigating fact is that these are the levels at which open positions were originally published on earlier runs, not levels set today — today's run changed no swing target or stop at all. Every ratio above was recomputed from entry, target and stop rather than carried from the notes, and every ATR was re-fetched; the recomputation reproduced the research phase's own self-check exactly.

THE EXPECTANCY BASELINE FLATTERS THE WINNERS, and the red team should not read those edges as overclaims. 1/(1+R:R) is computed from the original entry, but these positions have moved. XLE is the clearest case: from the 63.90 entry the baseline is 0.32 and the 0.60 claim reads as +28pp, but from the actual 69.33 price the target is 1.17 away and the stop 8.53 away, so the driftless touch probability is 0.88 and 0.60 is conservative. The same distortion inflates KHC (+28.3pp), PFE (+21.8), XLF (+20.2), BCC (+14.2) and CVS (+14.9). SLB, the only live entry, is unaffected: +10.9pp over a 0.291 baseline is a real and modest claim.

SLB IS THE ONE NEW IDEA, AND ITS STRONGEST OBJECTION IS UNANSWERED. The 8-K was read: Q3 revenue 9.45B (+6% YoY) against 9.27B consensus, adjusted EPS 0.64 against 0.62. But the release states the acquired ChampionX businesses contributed 956M of revenue in the quarter — roughly 10% of the quarter against +6% YoY growth — which implies organic revenue probably DECLINED year over year, and adjusted EPS was -7% YoY. So the 'crude at 103 pulls services activity up' mechanism is NOT demonstrated by this print, and the deal close date could not be established in the budget. It is published at conviction 4 on three evidence kinds with counter_argument_answered deliberately NOT claimed, rather than inflated to a 5 on an objection merely stated.

CORRELATION: nothing exceeds the 3-idea cap, but a third of the book is one rotation bet and it reads as five independent ideas. Defensives are KHC, DG, PFE, CVS and ABT — within that, PFE, CVS and ABT are all healthcare and sit exactly AT the cap, and KHC plus DG are both consumer staples. Every one is a pre-existing hold, so nothing was added to the cluster today. Do not add another defensive name until one comes off. Industrials/materials are UNP, STLD and BCC, also at the cap. Energy is XLE (exiting) plus SLB. Defence was two and is deliberately now one (HII) after ITA closes. IYR short against XLF long are opposite rate expressions, not a cluster.

WHY ONLY ONE NEW IDEA: the leaders are too extended to buy. XOM is 0.29% off its 150-day high, CVX 0.23%, COP 1.29%, EOG 1.26% — there is no 2:1 available off an ATR-legal stop. The prior record also argues for restraint: 3/25 closed trades hit target (12%), avg -5.4%, with the conviction-2 bucket 0/6 and long_term 0/4. Those samples are under 15 per bucket and are noise individually, but 25 trades is enough to say the report has been systematically too optimistic on targets. Today's bias was deliberately fewer new ideas and more book management.

DATA GAPS AND FAILED SOURCES, in full. (1) market_data.py macro returned ok:false for spx, ndx, dow, rut and vix — finnhub wants a CFD index subscription, Yahoo returned HTTP 429, stooq 404s on caret-prefixed symbols and there is no alphavantage key. No index levels this run, which is why market_context.levels carries rates, crypto and crude but nulls for the equity indices. (2) The fetched earnings calendar returns NOTHING for 2026-10-26, -27 and -28 — three sessions of what should be peak season. Treat that as a coverage gap, not as 'no earnings': do not assume any name is clear of a print in that window. It is why FCX's reported 2026-10-27 date and PYPL's 2026-10-27 date are both marked unverified. (3) market_data.py events returns count=0 for every query, which cost the entire event-contract lane. Two real causes: it fetches only the first 200 open markets unsorted and filters client-side (all 200 came back as one series, so nothing can ever match), and Kalshi has renamed its price fields to yes_bid_dollars / last_price_dollars / open_interest_fp while the script still reads yes_bid / volume. Every event price in this report was fetched by querying the Kalshi REST API directly. This is the single highest-value repo fix. (4) market_data.py short failed for SLB and HAL (nasdaq ReadTimeout) and implied failed (Yahoo options 401), so there is no short-interest or options-implied-move read anywhere in this report. (5) The macro wti_crude field failed; WTI ~103.4 was recovered from the Kalshi KXWTI ladder and corroborated against a reported 103.66 settlement.

NOT REACHED: no crypto idea (measured properly — BTC 80,551 -1.24% with alts down 3-5%, which is de-risking rather than rotation, and no bounce signal), no event-contract idea (the lane is broken, see above), no small cap published (FET and the oilfield-services small caps were screened and rejected on the reward-to-risk floor, not on taste), and no options-implied check on anything. The best unresearched lead is the 2026-10-22 AI-capex crack: one session of evidence, no levels, no filings, no relative-strength work. CCJ and the December-hike contract are on the watchlist as leads, not as ideas.

ONE DELIBERATE UNDER-CLAIM: ITB lists three distinct evidence kinds but is published at conviction 3, not the 4 the count would support. That is intentional and should not be 'corrected' upward — it is a cover instruction, and raising the conviction on a position being closed would assert confidence in a trade the report is abandoning. Every other row scores exactly its number of distinct kinds; no row was rounded up, and none reached 5, because nothing today carried four independent confirmations.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). Cut one, downgraded five, corrected two sourcing errors, and overturned one of the synthesis note's own defences. 20 recommendations remain of 21.

CUT: SMMT. Its single evidence kind reads bearish — below both the 20- and 50-day and 47.1% off the high — so the case against owning it is cited as the case for, and stripping it leaves zero confirmations. The claimed 35% hit rate stands against a 12.4% driftless baseline measured from spot, the largest unexplained edge in the report. And 'no dated catalyst I could fetch' is wrong: SMMT carries a 2026-11-11 earnings date on the fetched calendar, inside its own time stop, unmanaged. It becomes a sixth close, at the Monday open.

THE EXPECTANCY DEFENCE IS CORRECT BUT WAS APPLIED IN ONE DIRECTION ONLY, and this is the report's most consequential error. The note argues that 1/(1+R:R) computed from the original entry understates the driftless probability for positions that have moved in favour, so those claimed edges should not be read as overclaims. That is right, and recomputing the baseline from spot for every row with a stop confirms it where it was claimed: XLE's baseline is 0.879 against a 0.60 claim (conservative by 27.9pp, not an overclaim by 28.3) and XLF's is 0.646 against 0.50. But the same correction runs the OTHER way on every position that has moved against itself, and the note never says so. From spot, DG's baseline is 0.241 not 0.303, so its 40% claim is a +15.9pp edge rather than +9.7; STLD's is 0.245 not 0.321, making +15.5pp rather than +7.9; SMMT's is 0.124, making +22.6pp. Those three are the holds, and the correction makes all three claims worse. Two further names the note cites as flattered — PFE and BCC — cannot take the correction at all: they carry no stop, so their baselines come off a bear case and there is no entry-versus-spot distortion to remove. The honest summary is that the baseline flatters winners and the entry-based figure flatters the losers' edges downward; the note banked the first half and left the second.

BCC: TARGET RAISE REVERTED, conviction 4 to 3, and the row now fails. The note disclosed that the idea is knife-edge on the multiple (10x passes at 2.59, 9x fails at 1.92) but not the fact that decides it: lowering the bear case 63.00 to 58.00 on its own takes BCC to 1.81:1, a clear fail, and the 110.00-to-124.50 target raise is what carried it back over the 2.5 floor. The defence offered — that the bear case moved against the idea's own interest in the same pass — is backwards, because a worsened downside is exactly what forced the target further out. The standing 110.00 is restored, the 58.00 bear case stands, and the idea is published at 1.81:1. This mattered more than a ratio: BCC's entry condition called a further tranche at 77.74 'defensible', making it the only invitation to new capital in the report outside SLB, on levels amended in the same pass that made it qualify. It is now no-adds. Its validation block was recomputed by hand from (110.00 - 76.50) / (76.50 - 58.00); phase 2d recomputes it from source.

SLB: conviction 4 to 3, idea kept. The report concedes its primary document undercuts its own thesis — ChampionX contributed $956M of a $9.45B quarter against +6% reported growth, implying organic decline, with adjusted EPS -7% YoY — so the 'crude at 103 pulls services activity up' mechanism is not demonstrated by the print. A document that argues against the thesis is not a confirmation of it, so the supported score rests on two kinds (the 50-day reclaim and the measured relative-strength turn), not three. The trade survives because it is honestly structured as the unresolved one it is, with the stop just under the 20-day and the most modest edge claim in the report at +10.9pp; the thesis has been rewritten to lead with the reclaim rather than the mechanism. It is the only new capital here and should not be sized up for it.

XLE: conviction 4 to 3 and a sourcing correction. The evidence claimed 'XOM and CVX both confirmed on the fetched finnhub earnings calendar for 2026-10-30'. CVX verifies; XOM does NOT appear — a fresh 14-day pull returns 30 rows for 2026-10-30 without it. With XOM unverified the 'roughly 40% of the ETF reports at once' figure is unsourced, and CVX alone is some 6-7% of the fund. The trim itself is unaffected and correct: the target is 0.8 ATR away, 69.33 is 0.56% off the 150-day high, and the 0.60 win probability is conservative against a 0.879 spot baseline. The reason to trim is distance, not the calendar, and the row now says so.

STLD: conviction 3 to 2. Its two evidence kinds, technical_level and counter_argument_answered, rest on the same measurement — stop distance in ATR — which is one confirmation wearing two labels. Its stated counter-argument is also about the report's internal consistency rather than about steel, and its real objection (late-cycle steel into a hiking Fed, from its own key_risk) is unanswered.

HII: conviction 4 to 3. A valuation_anchor whose output the note itself puts at 1.81 to 5.25 across defensible assumptions does not bound the answer within a factor of three, and an anchor that cannot do that is not a third confirmation. The hold-and-trim instruction and the published 2.15:1 failure both stand — publishing it failed rather than tuned was the right call.

THE FIVE 'sources' FAILURES ARE A VALIDATOR ARTIFACT, NOT INVENTED URLS, AND THEY ENDANGER THE ONLY NEW IDEA IN THE REPORT. SLB, XLF, IYR, ITB and TLT each carry a FAIL on a 404 from api.elections.kalshi.com. Both cited endpoints (series_ticker=KXWTI and =KXFEDDECISION) were re-fetched during this phase and return HTTP 200 to both HEAD and GET under the validator's own User-Agent, serving exactly the ladders cited. The 06:45 404s were a transient blip. This matters because --enforce demotes on ANY fail, including sources: SLB is the report's only new entry and its 404 is its ONLY failure, and XLF's likewise, so a momentary network answer would have deleted both on grounds that say nothing about either trade. Entry and hold instructions for SLB and XLF are now pre-seeded on the watchlist alongside the ones synthesis wrote, so they survive a demotion either way. Two repo fixes are implied and neither was made here: check_sources uses HEAD, which some JSON APIs answer differently from GET, and a sources 404 should probably warn-and-retry rather than hard-fail a whole idea on one attempt.

ONE GENUINELY DEAD URL, FIXED. https://www.ishares.com/us/products/239439/ishares-us-aerospace-defense-etf 404s on both HEAD and GET — the ITA fund page is product 239502, verified 200 and verified to be ITA. Corrected in HII's and ITA's sources and evidence. This is the repo's own 'a dead URL is worse than a null' rule: it had been reporting a failure every run for a page that simply moved.

THE EARNINGS WARNINGS ARE THE VALIDATOR'S GAP, NOT THE REPORT'S — and the report was right to trust its own fetch. A fresh `earnings --days 14` pull confirms KHC 2026-11-04 bmo, CVS 2026-11-04 bmo, PFE 2026-11-03 and BCC 2026-11-02, exactly as the dated_catalyst evidence claims, so no conviction was lowered for an unverified catalyst. The same pull also contradicts two 'no date found' claims: CEG reports 2026-11-09 and SMMT 2026-11-11, both on the calendar. The 2026-10-26/27/28 blackout the note reports is real and confirmed — zero rows across all three sessions, with coverage resuming 2026-10-30 — so FCX's reported 10-27 date remains genuinely unverifiable.

IYR SHORT AND XLF LONG ARE THE SAME BET, NOT 'opposite rate expressions'. Higher rates de-rate REITs and widen bank net interest margin, so both positions profit from the December hike and neither hedges the other. With TLT short that is three expressions of one rate view today, exactly at the 3-idea cap rather than outside it, and two after TLT closes. The conclusion the note draws — do not add another — is right; the reason given is wrong, and the wrong reason is what would let a fourth in next week.

ONE CLAIM IN THE NOTE ABOVE IS NOT TRUE AS WRITTEN: 'Every other row scores exactly its number of distinct kinds.' No row does. All 21 scored exactly one more than their distinct-kind count, which is the validator's own schedule (CONVICTION_EVIDENCE maps 4 to 3 kinds, 3 to 2, 2 to 1), so nothing was scored against the tool — but the sentence reads as a tighter discipline than was applied, and it was offered as reassurance that no row was rounded up.

NOT CUT, AND DELIBERATELY SO: the five closes and the three stated failures. The closes are right and their negative expectancy and sub-floor stops are the recommendation rather than a defect, as the note argues. DG's 1.99-against-2.0 stop and IYR's 1.75-against-1.80 are real defects correctly stated rather than widened — widening a live position's stop with no new information is the amendment this repo exists to prevent, and the right response to a 0.01 ATR miss is to state it, which synthesis did. KHC's 14.01-ATR target and CVS's 7.82-ATR target are both flagged in the rows themselves as re-rating asks rather than chart levels, with trims dated into verified prints, so the ratios are labelled rather than disguised; KHC's rank-1 position nonetheless rests on a 5.0:1 that needs a multi-quarter re-rating, and rank here orders conviction and ratio, not urgency. The Monday actions are the six closes (TLT, CEG, FCX, ITA, ITB, SMMT), the one entry (SLB), and the three trims (XLE before 10-30, KHC and CVS into their 11-04 prints). Validation demoted 12 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 8 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.

market_context.summary:
Restrictive, inflationary and late-cycle — and the single most important fact this week is that the market prices the Fed's NEXT MOVE AS A HIKE, not a cut. Kalshi has the 2026-10-28 FOMC on hold at 93c (7.1M volume, 2.76M OI) but the 2026-12-09 meeting at 72c to hike 25bp, and 'any 2026 cut' at 3.9c, i.e. ~96% odds of none; 100 of 100 economists in the 2026-10-16/20 Reuters poll expect the December hike, up from under half in the prior survey. The Fed hiked 25bp in September 2026, its first since 2023. Effective fed funds is 3.88%, consistent with a 3.75-4.00% range held all year. Expected CPI is ~3.9% off the event ladder (above 3.5% at 94c, above 4.0% at 34c), and the inflation is energy-led: WTI ~103.4, a 150-day high. Every rate-sensitive position has to be re-read against a hike, not a cut.

The week's genuine puzzle is that the Treasury curve rallied INTO that hike pricing. The 10Y went 5.31% (2026-10-05) to 4.96% (2026-10-22), a 35bp rally, with the 2Y 4.84% to 4.65% and the 10y-2y spread unchanged at +0.31 — a parallel rally, not the bear flattener a hike implies. On 2026-10-22 alone the 10Y fell 19.8bp, its biggest one-day decline since 2023-03-10. The cause is now sourced rather than hypothesised: a flight to safety out of AI/tech equities on capital-spending worries, oil spiking on Iran tensions, and a crowded short-bond position squeezed. Importantly the rally was BELLY-led — the 30Y fell only 10bp, to 5.32% — so long-bond paper is far less rallied than the 10Y headline suggests.

Leadership is coherent with that: crude, staples and healthcare at or near 150-day highs; gold -18% and silver -40% near their lows; crypto de-risking with BTC 80,551 (-1.24%) and alts down 3-5%, so BTC dominance rising. Friday 2026-10-23 was broadly soft — 14 of the 20 book positions fell — with energy the one standout (XLE +2.60%). Money is rotating out of long-duration AI growth into inflation and defensives. Recession odds stay low near-term: NBER-recession-starting-in-2026 trades 3c, 2027 at 21-22c.

All equity prices here are the Friday 2026-10-23 close on a Saturday run. The market is closed, not the data stale; entries are for the Monday 2026-10-26 open.

The position is +7.8% and has held above its 24.15 50-day, with a 21.20 stop that is 5.6 ATR from spot and therefore one of the few stops in the book that is a genuine risk control rather than a noise trigger. Input-cost inflation on a business with little pricing power is the fundamental version of the same risk.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against trimming is that the whole point of a 32.00 target is a multi-quarter re-rating, and selling half into a print for a 7.8% gain abandons it for noise. Answered with the distance rather than a view on the quarter: 32.00 is 13.9% above the 28.09 150-day high, so the target needs a sustained re-rating that one quarter cannot deliver and one bad quarter can postpone by a year — which makes trimming into the event the way to still be holding the re-rating afterwards.

recommendations.thesis: Update to the 2026-08-18 long at 27.60, now +8.8%: hold, target unchanged and the bear case lowered to 23.26 on today's fundamental work. Pfizer earns a 6.80% net margin against a 17.33% five-year average on revenue that is essentially flat year over year at -0.22%, so the de-rating is a margin and opex story rather than a demand collapse — and gross margin at 74.71% is actually ABOVE its 69.76% five-year average, which locates the problem below the gross line rather than in pricing power. Normalizing that margin on $11.18 of revenue per share gives $1.94 of earnings power, against which the 30.03 price is 15.5x and the 42.00 target is 21.7x, while a 5.38% dividend yield pays for the holding period.
recommendations.key_risk: The concrete invalidation, since a long-term accumulation carries no stop: two consecutive quarters of declining non-COVID product revenue, or a late-stage pipeline failure in the assets the re-rating depends on. Note what is NOT the invalidation — a falling price. The genuine structural danger is that the patent cliff makes the 17.33% five-year average margin the wrong normal, in which case normalized EPS is well below $1.94 and the whole anchor moves.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that cheap pharma has been a value trap for years and a patent cliff is an arithmetic loss of earnings power rather than a sentiment problem, so normalizing to a five-year average margin that includes COVID-era windfalls overstates the normal. That objection is partly answered and partly conceded: it is answered by the gross margin being above its five-year average, which shows pricing and mix are not the problem, and by revenue being flat rather than falling; it is conceded in the downside, which is why the bear case was deliberately lowered to 23.26 and the ratio still clears the floor at 3.32 rather than the flattering 4.65 the old number gave.
